transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (NexaHealth, Head of ML), Jordan Lee (Platform Eng), Priya Raman (Security)

Auto-generated summary: Weekly POC check-in - onboarding items mostly in progress, waiting on credentials + security docs; SE ran initial latency baseline on small test; discussed Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for compliance and perf.

Topics: onboarding progress; access (service account, Terraform); Dedicated cluster provisioning; perf baseline; KV cache and batching; security/SOC2 + KMS; next steps + performance run schedule.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll start. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Torres: Hey, Maya here.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:12] Priya Raman: Priya on security.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood, SE. Avery's on the AE side.

[00:30] Avery: Agenda: onboarding progress, access setup, environment readiness, Samir will share initial perf notes, then next steps. Any other items?
[00:37] Maya: No, that's fine. Would like to focus on the Dedicated env creds and timeline.

[01:05] Samir: Quick sync on what we ran this week. We provisioned a small Dedicated test - 4 GPUs - ran a latency baseline for your sample prompts. Observed median token latency around 85ms on gpus, tail at 220ms for long sequences, but this is local short test, need full traffic run. Also saw some KV cache misses on session resets.
[01:28] Jordan: When you say KV cache misses, is that because of our session pattern? We're doing short lived sessions with a lot of new contexts.
[01:34] Samir: Yeah looks like prefix caching helps if there's reuse. For your pattern (lots of fresh contexts) batching and model quantization will matter more. Also suggested to tune batch windows to 40-50ms to trade a bit of latency for throughput.

[02:10] Priya: On security - we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and SSO (SAML). Any blockers on Redwood side?
[02:20] Avery: We can share SOC2 and ISO docs today - I'll drop links, and we support customer KMS in Dedicated + Private. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we'll provide SSO via an identity proxy, but need your IdP metadata.
[02:38] Maya: Great, we'll send the IdP metadata. Also we need network details - VPC peering or a private endpoint?
[02:45] Samir: For Dedicated we usually do VPC peering or customer-managed VPN. We'll send the VPC onboarding checklist. For on-prem/air-gapped we have Redwood Private but that's a longer process.

[03:20] Jordan: On Terraform state - we need to automate provisioning. Will you need access to our TF state bucket?
[03:25] Avery: We typically ask for a service account with least privilege and optionally temporary access to the TF state. If you prefer, we can provide IaC templates and you run them.

[03:50] Samir: Back to perf, there's one caveat: we used a quantized model variant for cheaper tokens, saw small quality delta on long-form completion, so we recommend a quick eval on your 50 test prompts to validate quality vs cost.
[04:07] Maya: That's important. We'll schedule evals. Any immediate tuning knobs?
[04:12] Samir: Batching window, KV cache TTL, and model variant (16-bit vs 8-bit). Also wire up prefix caching for repeated context. I can send a tuning checklist.

[04:45] Priya: A question on logs - you mentioned audit logs earlier, do logs include raw prompts? Our policy says raw PII should never be kept.
[04:52] Avery: By default we redact sensitive fields and we can configure retention and redaction policies. For Dedicated you have control over retention and we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog. We'll share the logging spec.

[05:20] Jordan: On access - what's outstanding from our side?
[05:23] Samir: We need: (1) service account key for provisioning, (2) IdP metadata for SAML if you want SSO, (3) sample traffic profile and a small dataset for eval, (4) approval for us to run a 10k token/day performance run on your Dedicated test cluster.
[05:40] Maya: We can provide those; service account I'll own. Timeline - can we try to have creds by next Tue?
[05:45] Avery: Yes we'll aim for that.

[06:00] Samir: Quick note on cost/latency tradeoffs - if you need strict 50ms p50 we can size more GPUs or use lower batch windows but cost increases. For many of your product flows p95 at 200ms is acceptable and we can batch more for cost savings.
[06:20] Maya: Our success criteria: p50 under 120ms for short prompts, end-to-end throughput of X requests/min for peak - I'll attach numbers in slack.

[06:40] Priya: About encryption - KMS integration means keys stay in our cloud tenant?
[06:44] Avery: Yes, we support customer-managed keys so the key material never leaves your KMS.

[07:05] Jordan: Any dependencies for the perf run? Like specific model selection?
[07:10] Samir: We recommend starting with rwd-llama-70b-quant (example name) for throughput, or rwd-30b for tighter latency. We'll propose model variants in the tuning doc. Also we'll try a quantized variant to measure cost delta.

[07:40] Maya: On reporting - can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[07:44] Avery: Yep, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. We'll give you access to the sandbox console for the Dedicated test.

[08:10] Jordan: Security review - Priya will want to run a short questionnaire. How long does that usually take?
[08:16] Priya: 10-15 standard items, then maybe a call with a security eng.
[08:20] Avery: We can have our security lead join the follow-up. I'll include them on the docs we send.

[09:00] Samir: Tuning recap: I'll send an initial baseline report (latency percentiles, throughput, KV hit ratio) and a tuning checklist. Plan: run a full traffic perf run after you provide sample traffic (target week of 2026-04-27).

[09:25] Maya: Sounds good. A few small points: we have regulatory requirement for data residency in US-east, so Dedicated needs to be in that region.
[09:33] Samir: Noted - we'll pin region and ensure model variants available there.

[10:00] Avery: Ok let's capture next steps and action items. I'll email SOC2 + ISO docs and VPC checklist today. Samir will provision credentials and run baseline once creds are in. Jordan will share traffic profile and grant TF access. Maya to confirm residency and provide IdP metadata.

[10:25] Maya: One last ask - can you also share a short runbook for failover? We need to understand graceful degradation and fallback options.
[10:32] Samir: Yes, we'll include the rollback and fallback policies and model variant fallback rules in the runbook.

[11:00] Avery: Recap: Docs sent, creds by next Tue, perf run scheduled week of 4/27, security review to start once docs received. Next sync same time next week?
[11:12] Maya: Works for us.
[11:15] Priya: Works.
[11:20] Jordan: Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had occasional mislabels (rwd-llama vs rwd-lama etc.) and some words like 'KV cache' transcribed as 'KV cash'.

References / Shared artifacts: Redwood SOC2 + ISO deck (link: https://redwood.example/soc2.pdf), VPC onboarding checklist (link: https://redwood.example/vpc-checklist), initial baseline report (to be shared by Samir).

End of meeting.
